description: One versioned model catalogue, read by the Rust runtime and by the drawing (ADR 0115, scoped by ADR 0120). A row records what a vendor's documentation says about a model, with the source and the read-date that docs/PROVIDERS.md requires of every row it publishes. It is NOT a capability: what this build can operate is core::providers::model_capabilities, and neither answer is derived from the other. Nothing outside this file spells a model id; consumers name a row by its id, which is a stable slug rather than a model name, so a vendor's next generation is a change to model_id here and nowhere else.

models.note: Groq's speech endpoint is batch only: one file in, one result out, no websocket and no stream=true.

models.note: The cleanup default this build ships. A REASONING MODEL, which is why the effort column exists: without `reasoning_effort` it spends the whole completion budget thinking and returns an empty string — measured at 46 reasoning tokens against a 48-token title budget. At `low` it thinks 10-56 tokens and answers in ~180 ms, the fastest of the chat models Groq serves as of this read. It still returns empty on some very short inputs; `normalize_correction` catches that as `empty_correction_fallback` and the dictation keeps its raw text.

models.note: Offered, not defaulted. The only row whose reasoning genuinely switches OFF — it never returns empty, and it sets punctuation and capitalization where the gpt-oss rows leave them alone. It is not the default because it INVENTS on broken input: `Bei c a u d e code` came back `Bei Caudé Code`, which is the failure mode docs/known-issues/cleanup-invents-tokens-on-broken-input.md is about and which the regression corpus has an entry for. Without `reasoning_effort: none` it writes its whole `<think>` block into the content.
The vendor documents this model as explicitly not streaming, while gpt-4o-transcribe on the same key does. That pair is ADR 0110's evidence.

models.note: The id this lane substitutes onto, because it is the one on the vendor's transcription page whose upstream every provider behind OpenRouter serves. Streaming is `unknown` rather than `unsupported`: the vendor documents no streaming transcription, and what the model behind the id does is its upstream's answer, not this build's — the third value ADR 0110 exists for, on the lane it was written about.

The same weights `openai-speech-gpt-4o-transcribe` names, and a SEPARATE row rather than an alias. The id differs, the credential differs, and the ceiling differs — OpenRouter documents 25 MB on the multipart path and a 60-second upstream timeout where OpenAI documents 25 MiB and no such cut. ADR 0110 keeps the answer per (provider, model) for exactly this case.
The cheaper half of the pair above.

models.note: The drawn name rather than a request id: there is no adapter and no request shape, and docs/PROVIDERS.md open disagreement 7 records that no published figure backs the 240 ms drawn beside it. The row exists so the three surfaces that draw this preset stop spelling it three times; each of them draws the vendor label in front of it.

82M parameters, Apache-2.0, StyleTTS 2 with an ISTFTNet vocoder. Its runtime is Python, which is a cost to price with the local speech runtime rather than separately — and the reason this row is drawn as an option and operated by nothing.
